chapter: Learning the drums and early influences
title: Playing breaks on 'I'm Nuts About Screwy Music'
summary: Crouch asks about the breaks on Lunceford recordings; Crawford says they were written in as four-bar or two-bar breaks and he just played them.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Now, was there-- so now, you -- you weren't taking any solos then.
No, I was no good at (inaudible) a solos, breaks either, just played straight runs.

Now, like -- I know, now, I have -- I was listening to some recordings (with the inaudible) band recently, like -- I mean I was recently listening to recordings, and they were those tunes like, for instance, 'I'm Nuts About Screwy Music.' You play --
I'm nuts about screwy music, ba-ba-dee-doo-ba-ba-ba-dee, da.
And you played some great -- like a lot of the recordings I have, you played a lot of breaks.
Oh, well, that was an occasion, you know. I just got enough nerve when they had -- when you got to do it, I had to do it.
So now, did you -- did transfer ask you to start playing breaks?
No. He didn't, just was on the arrangements. So I played them.
Now, were they written or did you --
No (Inaudible) they said four bar break, two bar break, something like that, and that's the way it happened.
